honesty: This index's LIST is now SIGNED: a detached raw Ed25519 signature over the EXACT served bytes of this file is published beside it as catalog.json.sig, and the Store verifies it in-page against the curator key pinned in index.html (CATALOG_PUBKEY_B64), rendering VERIFIED. That signature proves only that the LIST came from Postern's curator key; it does NOT, and cannot, attest any upstream app binary. Every HOSTED per-app artifact below is still UNBUILT: its checksum and signing.signature stay null with signing.state = "unpublished" until a real build runs — the pmOS apk mirrors need a Linux/pmbootstrap build host (see pmos-overlay/HONESTY.md), the attestable-nix entries need the Postern OS Nix closure. A proprietary app can only ever be linked or proxied — it is structurally impossible for hosted_by_us to be true when license.class is "proprietary". The 'attestable' badge is reserved for tier = attestable-nix (built from source inside the reproducible Postern OS Nix closure); a signed apk mirror is NOT attestable.

index_signature.note: A DETACHED raw Ed25519 signature (64 bytes) over the EXACT served bytes of this file, published beside it as catalog.json.sig. The Store verifies it in-page with SubtleCrypto against the curator public key pinned in index.html as CATALOG_PUBKEY_B64 (identical to pubkey_b64 here) and renders VERIFIED. 'signature' stays null in-band because the signature is detached — it cannot sign over bytes that contain itself. Proves the LIST came from Postern's curator key; it does not, and cannot, attest each upstream app's binary. The private half is never committed (see pmos-overlay/keys/postern-keygen.sh).

source.native-linux: Upstream native Linux build (from source or upstream binary).
source.flatpak: Flathub / flatpak remote — sandboxed desktop app.
source.fdroid: F-Droid — reproducible, FOSS-only Android repo (F-Droid signs).
source.waydroid-android: Android app run in Waydroid, or its upstream APK — user brings their own.
source.web: Runs in the browser / self-hosted web app; nothing to install locally.
source.postern-apk: Alpine/pmOS apk that WE build+sign and host in the Postern overlay repo.

tier.attestable-nix: Built from source inside the reproducible Postern OS Nix closure. The ONLY tier that earns the 'attestable' badge.
tier.pmos-overlay: Signed apk we host in the pmOS overlay. Proves who published it, NOT what it was built from. Not reproducible, not attestable.
tier.sloboda-compat: Android app reached via F-Droid, Waydroid, or the upstream APK. Trust chains to F-Droid or the upstream signer, not to us.
tier.browser: Web/self-hosted app opened in a browser. We host no binary; you run it or your own server does.

license_class.permissive: MIT / BSD / Apache-2.0 — redistribute and rebrand both allowed.
license_class.weak-copyleft: MPL-2.0 / LGPL — file/library-level copyleft; redistribute freely, rebrand allowed if modified files stay open.
license_class.strong-copyleft: GPL / AGPL — redistribute freely; a rebranded fork must ship its full source under the same license.
license_class.proprietary: Closed source. We may never host or rebrand it — link or proxy to the vendor only.

distribution_model.attest: Built from source in the Postern OS Nix image; verity-sealed. hosted_by_us=true.
distribution_model.mirror: We host an unmodified copy of the upstream binary as a signed apk. hosted_by_us=true.
distribution_model.overlay-build: We build from source via an APKBUILD and host the signed apk. hosted_by_us=true.
distribution_model.link: We only point at the upstream source (Flathub / F-Droid / vendor). hosted_by_us=false.
distribution_model.proxy: We host a manifest/wrapper that fetches the upstream binary at install time — never the binary itself. hosted_by_us=false.

vocab.rebrand_vs_redistribute: redistribute = may we host the upstream binary as-is? rebrand = may we fork the source and ship it under Postern branding? Trademark can forbid using the upstream NAME/logo even when the license permits redistribution (Firefox/Thunderbird/Signal are the classic cases): those we link rather than mirror. Proprietary forbids both.

apps.name: Postern Vault
apps.oneliner: First-party secrets/password vault, sealed with one canonical AEAD (XChaCha20-Poly1305 + Argon2id), software keystore — unaudited.

license.note: Our own code; permissive by repo rule (deny.toml forbids GPL/AGPL).

distribution.verify: Reproducible Nix build; verity-sealed in the Postern OS image.

privacy.stays: Secrets, encrypted at rest, never leave the device.
privacy.leaves: Nothing.

apps.limits: Built & tested at the crate level; the end-user UI is the remaining app layer.

apps.name: Postern Courier
apps.oneliner: First-party serverless file drop over an ephemeral Tor onion, payload sealed post-quantum.

license.note: Our own permissive code.

distribution.verify: Reproducible Nix build; verity-sealed in the Postern OS image.

privacy.stays: File contents — hybrid ML-KEM-sealed end-to-end to the recipient's key.
privacy.leaves: Only ciphertext transits the Tor circuit.

apps.limits: Sender must stay online for the live transfer; onion address crypto is classical.

apps.name: Postern OS Desktop
apps.oneliner: First-party privacy Linux declared in Nix: reproducible image, Tor by default, zero telemetry.

license.note: Our own Nix profile.

distribution.verify: Reproducible NixOS image; the root of the attestable tier.

privacy.stays: The OS sends nothing home: telemetry stripped, deny-inbound firewall, Tor client on.
privacy.leaves: Only traffic you generate.

apps.limits: A NixOS profile to iterate, not a frozen distro; the image is not built in this sandbox (labeled designed).

apps.name: KeePassXC
apps.oneliner: Offline password manager with a local KDBX database — no cloud, no account.

license.note: GPL permits a fork; the KeePassXC name/logo are the project's — a fork must be renamed. We build it unmodified in the Nix image.

distribution.verify: Built from source in the Postern OS Nix closure — the attestation is of OUR image build, not of upstream's own binaries.

privacy.stays: The KDBX vault stays on your device.
privacy.leaves: Nothing unless you enable browser integration or sync the file yourself.

apps.limits: The 'attestable' badge covers our reproducible Nix build only; on Flathub/native you trust that channel's signer instead.

apps.name: Syncthing
apps.oneliner: Continuous file sync directly between your own devices — no server in the middle.

license.note: MPL is file-level copyleft; redistribute freely. 'Syncthing' is a registered mark — a fork must drop the name.

distribution.verify: Built from source in the Postern OS Nix closure.

privacy.stays: Your files stay on the devices you own; transfers are TLS between them.
privacy.leaves: Metadata to global discovery/relay servers unless you disable them and pin device addresses.

apps.limits: Default discovery/relay servers see connection metadata; both are self-hostable.

apps.name: GIMP
apps.oneliner: Full raster image editor — a fully offline Photoshop alternative.

license.note: GPLv3+; a fork must rename off the GIMP mark.

distribution.verify: Built from source in the Postern OS Nix closure.

privacy.stays: Everything — image editing is entirely on-device.
privacy.leaves: Nothing.

apps.limits: Not a vector tool; heavy files want RAM. The attestation is of our Nix build only.

apps.name: VLC media player
apps.oneliner: Plays essentially any media file or stream, fully offline.

license.note: GPLv2+; redistribute freely. 'VLC' and the cone logo are VideoLAN marks — a fork must rename.

distribution.verify: We host a SIGNED apk (proves we published it) — NOT reproducible, NOT attestable. See pmos-overlay/HONESTY.md.

privacy.stays: Local playback stays on-device.
privacy.leaves: Only network streams you deliberately open.

apps.limits: Signed, not attestable: the signature proves the publisher, not that the binary matches source.

apps.name: LibreOffice
apps.oneliner: Complete offline office suite — documents, spreadsheets, presentations.

license.note: MPL-2.0; redistribute freely. 'LibreOffice' is a TDF mark — a fork must rename (as Collabora/OxOffice do).

distribution.verify: Signed apk in the Postern overlay — signed, not attestable.

privacy.stays: Your documents stay on the device.
privacy.leaves: Nothing unless you enable an online feature. Run Postern Hygiene before sharing — office files carry author/GPS metadata.

apps.limits: Signed, not attestable. Large suite — the pmOS build is heavy on mobile.

apps.name: OnionShare
apps.oneliner: Share files, host a site, or chat over your own temporary Tor onion service.

license.note: GPLv3; a fork must rename off the OnionShare mark.

distribution.verify: Signed apk in the overlay; upstream also publishes GPG-signed releases you can cross-check.

privacy.stays: Files and the service run on your own machine.
privacy.leaves: Only over the Tor circuit to the recipient's onion address.

apps.limits: Sender stays online during the transfer; Tor endpoint timing analysis remains out of scope.

apps.name: Cryptomator
apps.oneliner: Client-side encryption for any cloud folder — the provider only ever sees ciphertext.

license.note: Desktop app is GPLv3; a fork must rename. (The mobile apps carry their own terms upstream.)

distribution.verify: Signed apk in the overlay — signed, not attestable.

privacy.stays: Encryption keys and plaintext stay on the device.
privacy.leaves: Only encrypted vault files, to whatever cloud folder you point it at.

apps.limits: Protects file contents, not filenames-count/size metadata the cloud can still see.

apps.name: Mumble
apps.oneliner: Low-latency voice chat you can self-host — permissively licensed.

license.note: Permissive — redistribute and rebrand both allowed with attribution.

distribution.verify: Signed apk in the overlay — signed, not attestable.

privacy.stays: Your identity/certificate is local.
privacy.leaves: Voice + who-talks-to-whom to the server you connect to; run your own for control. Not end-to-end encrypted by default.

apps.limits: Transport is client↔server TLS, not end-to-end; the server operator can hear channels unless configured otherwise.

apps.name: Mozilla Thunderbird
apps.oneliner: Full desktop email client with built-in OpenPGP encryption.

license.note: MPL code is free, but the Thunderbird NAME + logo are Mozilla trademarks: we may NOT ship a 'Thunderbird'-branded build. So we LINK to Flathub, never mirror under the name. A rebranded fork must strip Mozilla branding.

distribution.verify: Install from Flathub; Flathub and Mozilla sign their builds. We host nothing.

privacy.stays: OpenPGP private keys and local mail store stay on-device.
privacy.leaves: Mail to/from your providers (SMTP/IMAP see everything unencrypted mail carries); PGP protects body, not headers/subject on older setups.

apps.limits: Trademark forces link-only: we can't distribute a build called Thunderbird. Email metadata is inherently exposed to providers.

apps.name: NewPipe
apps.oneliner: Watch YouTube and other sites with no Google account, ads, or background tracking.

license.note: GPLv3; a fork must rename off the NewPipe mark.

distribution.verify: Install from F-Droid, which builds from source and signs. We host nothing.

privacy.stays: No account, no watch history synced anywhere.
privacy.leaves: Your requests still reach the origin site (e.g. YouTube), which sees your IP and what you fetch.

apps.limits: Depends on scraping origin sites; breaks when they change. The origin still sees your IP/requests.

apps.name: Aegis Authenticator
apps.oneliner: Offline TOTP/HOTP two-factor codes in an encrypted local vault.

license.note: GPLv3; a fork must rename off the Aegis mark.

distribution.verify: Install from F-Droid; it builds and signs from source. We host nothing.

privacy.stays: All 2FA secrets — encrypted at rest on the device.
privacy.leaves: Nothing; codes are generated offline.

apps.limits: Back up your encrypted export yourself — there is no cloud recovery by design.

apps.name: Briar
apps.oneliner: Peer-to-peer messaging over Tor — or Wi-Fi/Bluetooth when the internet is down.

license.note: GPLv3; a fork must rename off the Briar mark.

distribution.verify: Install from F-Droid; upstream also publishes reproducible-build verification. We host nothing.

privacy.stays: Messages and contacts — stored encrypted on-device; no central server.
privacy.leaves: Only end-to-end encrypted traffic over Tor (or local radio); no phone number or account.

apps.limits: Both parties must add each other; no async delivery if neither device is reachable.

apps.name: Organic Maps
apps.oneliner: Offline maps and turn-by-turn navigation from OpenStreetMap — no tracking.

license.note: Apache-2.0 — permissive; the 'Organic Maps' name/logo are the project's, so a fork must rename.

distribution.verify: Install from F-Droid. We host nothing.

privacy.stays: Downloaded maps and your location stay on the device.
privacy.leaves: Nothing during navigation; only the map downloads you request.

apps.limits: Map data quality is whatever OpenStreetMap has for the area; no live traffic.

apps.name: Signal (Android)
apps.oneliner: Modern end-to-end encrypted messenger and calls; the client is open source.

license.note: Client is GPLv3, but 'Signal' is a registered mark and the Foundation asks that their build not be redistributed under the Signal name — so we LINK to the upstream APK, we do not mirror or rebrand it.

distribution.verify: Install the official APK from signal.org (or Play). We host nothing and do not rebrand it.

privacy.stays: Message contents — end-to-end encrypted; keys only on your devices.
privacy.leaves: Ciphertext plus minimal metadata to Signal's servers; registration needs a phone number.

apps.limits: Requires a phone number; runs in Waydroid on a Linux phone, not natively. FOSS client, but we link rather than repackage.

apps.name: Jitsi Meet
apps.oneliner: Self-hostable group video calls in the browser — no account, no install.

license.note: Apache-2.0 — permissive; a self-hosted deployment must drop the Jitsi trademark if rebranded.

distribution.verify: Run your own server, or use meet.jit.si. We host no instance.

privacy.stays: Nothing local to install.
privacy.leaves: Audio/video to whichever server hosts the room; the server sees participants. E2EE is optional and browser-dependent. Self-host for control.

apps.limits: On a shared public instance the operator is in the media path unless E2EE is on for every participant.

apps.name: Nextcloud
apps.oneliner: Self-hosted files, calendar, and collaboration — your own server, your data.

license.note: AGPL-3.0 — network copyleft: any modified server you expose must offer its source. 'Nextcloud' is a mark; a rebranded fork must rename.

distribution.verify: You (or a provider you choose) run the server. We host no instance and store none of your data.

privacy.stays: Whatever stays on the server you control.
privacy.leaves: Everything to the server operator — which is you if self-hosted, or your chosen provider otherwise.

apps.limits: Only as private as the server you run it on; AGPL applies if you expose a modified build.

apps.name: Spotify
apps.oneliner: Proprietary music streaming. Listed for reference — we can only link, never host.

license.note: Closed source. We may not host, mirror, or rebrand it under any circumstances — link or proxy only.

distribution.verify: Use the web player, or the community Flathub manifest that DOWNLOADS Spotify's own binary at install (a proxy — even Flathub hosts no binary). We host neither the binary nor a manifest.

privacy.stays: Nothing you can verify — it is closed source.
privacy.leaves: Account, listening history, and device telemetry to Spotify. This is not a private app; it is here so the catalog is honest about the boundary.

apps.limits: PROPRIETARY: closed binary, telemetry you cannot inspect. Structurally link/proxy only — the store will never host it.

apps.name: WhatsApp
apps.oneliner: Proprietary messenger. Listed for reference — bring your own; we can only link.

license.note: Closed source, Meta-owned. We may never host, mirror, or rebrand it — link only.

distribution.verify: Install the vendor's own APK / Play build inside Waydroid yourself. We host nothing and endorse nothing about its privacy.

privacy.stays: Message bodies are E2E encrypted, but that is Meta's own unverifiable claim.
privacy.leaves: Contacts, metadata (who/when/how often), and device signals to Meta. A phone number is required.

apps.limits: PROPRIETARY: closed source; message-content encryption is unverifiable and metadata is extensive. Structurally link-only.
